title: Polynomial-time iteration of shrinking functions
statement: Let $f$ and $s$ be polynomial-time computable functions on Boolean words, and let $N$ be a natural-valued function whose unary encoding is polynomial-time computable. If $f$ never increases word length, then the function mapping $x$ to the $N(x)$-fold iterate of $f$ applied to $s(x)$ is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: the unary encoding of $N(x)$ is polynomial-time computable
replaced: If a polynomial-time computable step function never increases word length, then for any polynomial-time initial-word and unary-count producers, the counted iterate is polynomial-time computable; repeated sequential projections and tail scans therefore need no random access.
